summary: Rabbi Yehudah lists six cases where Beis Shammai are easier and Beis Hillel are stricter, about blood of a neveilah, eggs, some kinds of tumah, shemittah fruit and a leather bottle.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
six things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: The blood of neveilos,
Beis Shammai say it is tahor,
and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.
An egg found inside a neveilah,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהּ נִמְכֶּרֶת בַּשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: if eggs like it are sold in the market,
it is allowed. And if not,
it is forbidden, like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel forbid it.
And they agree that an egg of a treifah is forbidden,
because it grew while forbidden.

chunks.he: דַּם נָכְרִית וְדַם טָהֳרָה שֶׁל מְצֹרַעַת,
chunks.en: A kind of tumah of a non-Jewish woman, and of a woman who is a metzora in her tahor days,

words.en: and a kind of tumah of

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is tahor.
And Beis Hillel say:
it is like her spit and her other liquids.
chunks.explain: It makes tamei only while it is wet.

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין פֵּרוֹת שְׁבִיעִית בְּטוֹבָה וְשֶׁלֹּא בְטוֹבָה,
chunks.en: We may eat shemittah fruit with or without thanks to the owner,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we eat only with thanks to the owner.
A leather bottle: Beis Shammai say:
only when it stands tied up.
And Beis Hillel say:
even when it is not tied up.

summary: Rabbi Yose lists six more cases where Beis Shammai are easier: chicken and cheese on the table, terumah from olives and grapes, planting in a vineyard, dough, a mikveh, and a ger on erev Pesach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yose says:
six things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: Chicken may be put together with cheese
on the table but it is not eaten together,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
it is not put up and it is not eaten.
We may take terumah from olives for oil,
and from grapes for wine,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we may not take terumah this way.
One who plants in the four amos of the vineyard,
Beis Shammai say:
he made one row forbidden,
chunks.explain: Kilayim: planting seeds near grapevines makes them forbidden.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say:
he made two rows forbidden.
A soft dough: Beis Shammai say it is free from challah,
and Beis Hillel say it must have challah taken.
We may dip in a flowing stream of rainwater,
like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
we may not dip there.
A ger who became Jewish on erev Pesach,
Beis Shammai say:
he dips in the mikveh and eats his Pesach offering in the evening.
And Beis Hillel say:
one who just had his bris
is like one who leaves a grave.
chunks.explain: He must wait seven days to become tahor.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael lists three cases where Beis Shammai are easier: Koheles, the water of the parah adumah, and a spice called ketzach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
three things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: Koheles does not make the hands tamei,
chunks.explain: Holy books make hands tamei; so is Koheles a holy book?

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Shammai.
And Beis Hillel say:
it makes the hands tamei.
Chatas water that was already used for its mitzvah,
Beis Shammai say it is tahor,
and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.

chunks.he: הַקֶּצַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַהֲרִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַמְּאִין.
chunks.en: Ketzach: Beis Shammai say it is tahor and Beis Hillel say it is tamei.

words.note: A kind of black seed used as a spice.

chunks.en: And the same for maaser.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer lists two cases where Beis Shammai are easier, about a kind of tumah of a woman after she has a baby.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
two things are among the easy rulings of Beis
Shammai and the strict rulings of Beis Hillel.

words.en: and from the strict rulings of

chunks.en: The tumah of a woman after birth who did not yet go to the mikveh,
Beis Shammai say:
it is like her spit and her other liquids.
And Beis Hillel say:
it makes tamei whether wet or dry.
And they agree that a woman after birth who has zivah, it

words.en: about a woman who gave birth

words.note: A kind of tumah that comes from the body.

chunks.en: makes tamei whether wet or dry.

summary: Four brothers, two married to two sisters. If those two die, the other brothers do chalitzah and may not marry them.

chunks.en: Four brothers,
two of them married to two sisters,
the ones married to the sisters died,
these women do chalitzah and do not marry the brothers.
And if they went ahead and married them,

chunks.he: יוֹצִיאוּ. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי,
chunks.en: they must send them away. Rabbi Eliezer says in the name of Beis Shammai:
they may keep them. And Beis Hillel say: they must send them away.

summary: Akavya ben Mahalalel would not take back four rulings, even to become the head of the beis din. The Mishnah tells what happened, and Rabbi Yehudah says Akavya was never put in cherem.

chunks.he: עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל הֵעִיד אַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים.
chunks.en: Akavya ben Mahalalel testified about four things.
They said to him:

chunks.he: עֲקַבְיָא, חֲזֹר בְּךָ בְאַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁהָיִיתָ אוֹמֵר
chunks.en: Akavya, take back the four things that you used to say,
and we will make you the head of the beis din of Yisrael.
He said to them:

chunks.he: מוּטָב לִי לְהִקָּרֵא שׁוֹטֶה כָּל יָמַי,
chunks.en: It is better for me to be called a fool all my days,
and not to be for one moment
wicked before Hashem,

words.note: Literally "the Place," a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: so that people should not say:
"He took it back for the sake of power."
He used to say that a "left" hair is tamei
of a spot of tzaraas, and a greenish kind of tumah.

words.note: A hair in a spot of tzaraas.
A kind of tumah of a woman.

chunks.en: And the Sages say they are tahor.
He used to allow the hair of a bechor
with a blemish that fell off and he put it in a window
and after that did shechitah on it,
and the Sages forbid.
He used to say:
we do not give the sotah water to drink, not to a woman who became a gerus
chunks.explain: A woman whose husband suspects her drinks special water.

words.en: the woman who became a ger

chunks.en: and not to a freed maidservant.
And the Sages say:
we do give them to drink. They said to him:
It happened with Karkemis,
a freed maidservant who was in Yerushalayim,
and Shemayah and Avtalyon gave her to drink.
He said to them:
They only gave her something that looked like it.
And they put him in cherem, and he died in his cherem,

words.en: and they put him in cherem
words.note: Kept away from the people as a punishment.

chunks.en: and the beis din put a stone on his coffin.
Rabbi Yehudah said:
Heaven forbid that Akavya was put in cherem,
because the Azarah was never locked on any

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: person in Yisrael as great in wisdom and fear of sin
as Akavya ben Mahalalel.
And whom did they put in cherem?
Eliezer ben Chanoch,
who doubted the washing of hands.
And when he died, the beis din sent and put
a stone on his coffin.
This teaches that anyone who is put in cherem and dies in his cherem,
we put a stone on his coffin.

summary: Before he died, Akavya told his son to follow the many Sages and not his own four rulings. He also taught his son that his own good deeds would bring him close to the Sages.

chunks.en: At the time of his death he said to his son:

chunks.he: בְּנִי, חֲזֹר בְּךָ בְאַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁהָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר.
chunks.en: My son, take back the four things that I used to say.
He said to him:
And why did you not take them back?
He said to him:
I heard it from the mouth of the many,
and they heard it from the mouth of the many.
I stood firm on what I heard,
and they stood firm on what they heard.
But you heard it from the mouth of one person,
and from the mouth of the many.
It is better to leave the words of the one,
and to hold on to the words of the many.
He said to him:
Father, speak well of me to your friends.
He said to him:
I will not ask them.
He said to him:
Maybe you found something wrong in me?
He said to him:
No. Your deeds will bring you close and your deeds will push you away.
